# 0013 — Web frontend: React + daisyUI on Bun, structure generated by Puerto, wire types from OpenAPI

**Status:** Accepted (2026-10-11 — built in 9.0, 9.1 and 9.2). Spec: `PLAN.md` § Phase 9.

## Context

Puerto generates the backend of a Rails-style scaffold but no screen. The frontend must (a) leave
a working CRUD per entity, (b) give the structure to keep developing by hand, (c) follow the same
Dependency Rule as the backend — the layout of nexe-document's `document-workspace` — and (d) stay
cheap for Puerto to keep green in the compile matrix.

Options weighed:

- **Leptos / Dioxus (WASM).** One language, but the DTOs are poem-openapi `Object`s, not serde, so
  sharing types is not free; a wasm target and trunk multiply `make test/full`; both frameworks
  break their API often enough to keep breaking the templates.
- **HTMX + Askama.** No build step, but HTML endpoints sit next to the JSON API inside
  `presentation` (API First is lost) and the HTML is checked by no contract.
- **TypeScript.** Bun enters the toolchain. Everything else is in its favour: the OpenAPI spec
  becomes the contract between the two halves, and agents write TS/React well.

A first draft copied document-workspace's four layers wholesale, one use case class per CRUD
action. Read against its own code (`list-queue-tasks.ts`: log, call the repository, return), a
frontend CRUD use case only delegates — the server owns validation — so that layer would be
generated empty five times per entity.

## Decision

- **React 19 + daisyUI 5 (Tailwind v4).** daisyUI is CSS classes only: no JS, no runtime
  dependency, works with native `<dialog>` and `<form>`, which is all a CRUD needs, and the user
  can swap it. shadcn was rejected for its dependency weight; Preact / Svelte for the friction of a
  compat layer or a second mental model.
- **No TanStack.** wouter for routing, a small `useAsync` hook for server state. Without file-based
  routing the route table is a **generated file** (`core/generated/routes.tsx`), so adding an
  entity never patches user code — the same move as `bootstrap.rs`.
- **Bun** as runtime, package manager and test runner (`bun test`): one binary to pin and install
  in CI, and the fastest install for a matrix that generates many projects.
- **No layer without logic.** The generated CRUD is `domain/` (types, error, repository port),
  `infrastructure/` (HTTP adapter) and `presentation/` (containers call the port, views take
  props). `application/` ships empty with a README: a use case is written by hand when there is a
  rule or an orchestration to hold, and Puerto never generates one. What the hexagon buys on the
  frontend is the port — screens tested against a fake repository, no network — plus one
  composition root (`core/generated/dependencies.ts`) and the Dependency Rule checked by
  dependency-cruiser.
- **Puerto generates the structure itself**, from puerto.toml and its Tera templates. It is *not*
  delegated to openapi-generator: that tool knows nothing of layers, and bending its mustache
  templates into them would be a second template system to maintain.
- **openapi-typescript generates only the wire types** (`infrastructure/http/schema.d.ts`), used
  through openapi-fetch by the generated adapters. A DTO changed in Rust — including by hand —
  fails `bun run typecheck`. The spec is exported by a Rust test from mocked use cases (ADR-0012)
  into a committed `docs/api/openapi.json`, so a contract change shows in the diff.
- **No client-side copy of domain rules.** The 422 code from the server is shown as-is. Sharing
  the rules themselves (the Rust domain compiled to WASM) is deferred to Phase 10, triggered by
  the first non-trivial validation rule — today puerto.toml already keeps both sides consistent
  at generation time.
- **Optional, default on**: `[project] web = true`, `puerto new --no-web` to skip.

## Consequences

- `make test/full` and CI need `bun`. A generated project needs it too, unless created with
  `--no-web`.
- Two steps after touching a DTO (`make web/sync`): Puerto never runs `cargo` or `bun` itself.
  Until the sync, the frontend does not typecheck — deliberate, it is the drift signal.
- A container that grows logic is the cue to move it into `application/`; nothing enforces it
  beyond review and the Dependency Rule.
- Accessibility beyond native elements (combobox, focus traps) is the user's to add — daisyUI
  ships none.
- `bun test` + happy-dom + testing-library is verified in piece 9.0; if it does not hold, Vitest
  (run by Bun) replaces it and this ADR records why.
- Puerto now owns templates in two languages; the snapshot files cover both.

## Verified in 9.0

- `bun test` + happy-dom (`@happy-dom/global-registrator`) + Testing Library holds: two preload
  files in `bunfig.toml`, happy-dom first, because Testing Library builds `screen` from
  `document` when it is imported. Vitest is not needed.
- The tool scripts run as `bun --bun <tool>`. dependency-cruiser refuses an odd-numbered Node
  release (it found Node 25 on `PATH`); under Bun's runtime it needs no Node at all.
- TypeScript stays on 5.x: `openapi-typescript` declares a `typescript ^5` peer, and TypeScript 7
  (the native port) has no JS API for dependency-cruiser to parse with.

## Decided in 9.1

- The spec test writes `docs/api/openapi.json` when it is **missing** and passes; only an existing,
  different file fails. Strict-on-missing would make a fresh `puerto new` fail `make test` with
  nothing to sync. The compile matrix runs the test twice (write, then compare), so the strict
  path and the determinism of the export stay covered.
- `openapi_service()` in `bootstrap.rs` is the only `OpenApiService::new`: the server adds
  `.server(...)` on top, the test calls `.spec()` on it. The exported spec carries no `servers`
  entry — the frontend's client uses `baseUrl: "/api"`.

## Decided in 9.2

- **`client.ts` comes with the first entity**, not the template. It imports `schema.d.ts`, which
  only exists after `make web/sync`; in the template it made a fresh `puerto new` fail
  `bun run typecheck`. The first scaffold needs a sync anyway. Written once, never overwritten.
- **Entities whose fields the frontend generator does not handle yet get no slice at all** (9.2
  covers `String`, `Uuid`, `i64`, `f64`, `bool` and non-enum VOs over them). The alternative — a
  slice that does not typecheck — would turn every intermediate project red; one predicate
  (`web::has_web_slice`) keeps scaffold, the guard, the drift check and `core/generated/*`
  agreeing on who has screens.
- **The bun checks run in every web scenario of the matrix**, not only `web_crud`: a few seconds
  each (install from a warm cache included) against minutes of `cargo`, and every scenario that
  later gains a slice is then checked by its own frontend.
- **Generated TypeScript is emitted Biome-clean**, not formatted afterwards: `bun run lint`
  checks it in the matrix before any formatting. Puerto never runs bun, so it emulates the two
  rules that depend on names — import order (`web::organize_imports`: sources by distance, `/`
  before other characters, specifiers case-insensitively) and wrapping at 100 columns where a
  line's length depends on the entity (routes, `navEntries`, wrapped imports). Templates avoid
  the rest by shape. Formatting cannot be emulated for every name, so `make web/sync` — the step
  every scaffold already needs — also runs `bun run format` (`biome check --write` with the
  linter off: formatting and import order only, a no-op on files that already pass `make lint`).
- **Screens are tested through `renderScreen(ui, dependencies, path)`** (`test-support/render.tsx`,
  template): a `Partial<Dependencies>` — a screen test names only the adapters it uses, so adding
  an entity does not touch other entities' tests — and a recording wouter memory location to
  assert navigation. `test-support/` may not reach an adapter, and only test files may import it
  (dependency-cruiser).
- **Variables named after the entity avoid TypeScript's reserved words** (`Case` → `caseItem`)
  and the templates' own locals; an uncountable plural (`series`) names its list `seriesList`.
